chapter: Learning the drums and early influences
title: Northern and southern drumming styles and Joe Jones with Basie
summary: Crawford contrasts the southern snare-and-choke style with the freer northern style and praises Joe Jones, subbing for him at the Club Harlem.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Now, you say that -- you say there was a -- now, you were saying earlier that there -- excuse me (there was) (inaudible) what you call a northern style and a southern style of drumming.
Well, there was the northern. You used the term northern style.
What would you term southern style?

Well, south ern style was strictly snare drum, choke cymbal, that sh-sh-chum-sh-sh-sh-sh, sh-sh-- chum, sh-sh-sh-h-h, you know, that style and snare drum. Northern style -- played more freely. Joe Jones (inaudible) was really -- he revolutionized the drums to me. He played so freely with Basie and smooth as silk. Occasionally, pardon me, (the Club Harlem) Basie would call me over. I was playing a club, played there for many summers.

And Basie, whenever Joe decided to play sick, wouldn't show up or something like that, Basie needed a drummer. So they had two drummers over at the Club Harlem. I didn't play no dance music. I strictly played the shows, which were about an hour or two long. I played the shows, so I went over and
played in Joe's place, subbed for him.
I don't know what year it was. It was later than that. What I mean, in the '40s, wasn't it?
I told him about Cafe Society.
Yeah, but go ahead. Now, but what were you saying about the northern style. You were saying that -- now, what was it that you -- that Joe Jones did -- to use the northern style?

Oh, Joe Jones revolutionized the new trend of drumming, freely, that silk style, (inaudible) the cymbal up here, brushes or sticks, and he played some tremendous breaks. I have a record here now about Basie, featuring Joe Jones. Old Man River -- Old Man -- let me see. He'd get in a part tempo, way up. He'd get in one part of that solo, and he started to playing it with his bass drum 4-4. Toogaloo-loo-loo-loo. And he had -- he just could play it to me.
